description: PREREQUISITE: flm-40e.2 (Item 1a) complete. VNodeCompiler already exists at lib/filament/vnode_compiler.ex — read it before starting. ── STEP 0: Fix LiveView bare-variable warning (apply first) ───────────────── VNodeCompiler.compile/2 currently passes the real caller env to Phoenix.LiveView.TagEngine.compile/2. TagEngine's engine.ex calls maybe_warn_taint/3 which checks Macro.Env.has_var?(caller, {name, nil}) — any variable defined in the enclosing scope triggers this warning: "you are accessing the variable X inside a LiveView template. Using variables in HEEx templates are discouraged as they disable change tracking." This is a false positive. Filament intentionally uses lexical scoping; the LiveView __changed__ mechanism is irrelevant to Filament's fiber reconciler. Fix: in lib/filament/vnode_compiler.ex, strip vars from caller before passing to TagEngine. TagEngine uses caller only for this warning check; file and line are passed as separate options. # Before calling TagEngine: sanitized_caller = %{caller | vars: []} quoted = Phoenix.LiveView.TagEngine.compile(source, file: caller.file, line: caller.line + 1, caller: sanitized_caller, # stripped, not caller indentation: 0, tag_handler: Filament.HTMLEngine ) Apply this change first. Verify: recompile the collaboration example (examples/collaboration/) and confirm the warning is gone. ── STEP 1: Reactive scope inference ───────────────────────────────────────── WHAT PROBLEM THIS SOLVES Without memoization, every render re-evaluates every sub-expression even if inputs have not changed. React Compiler (React Forget) solves this by grouping template sub-expressions into reactive scopes by shared dependencies, each getting its own cache slot. Filament does the same at compile time in VNodeCompiler. TERMINOLOGY reactive variable: any @foo reference (bare variable after Item 1a transform) reactive scope: a sub-expression whose deps are a specific subset of reactive variables stable value: does not change across renders — use_state setters, atoms, integers, literals KEY INSIGHT: use_state setters are stable (guaranteed by Item 0, flm-40e.1). Closures that capture ONLY stable values are themselves stable and can be memoized with [] deps (computed once, never recomputed). DEPENDENCY TRACKING ALGORITHM At compile time, for each sub-expression in the template AST: 1. Walk the AST to collect all variable references 2. Identify which are reactive (appear as @foo references in the template) 3. Closures: their deps are the reactive variables they capture (exclude stable setter vars) 4. Group adjacent sub-expressions with identical dep sets into one scope 5. Each scope: use_memo(deps, fn -> end) STABLE SETTER DETECTION Pattern-match on binding sites at the call site: {count, set_count} = use_state(_) → count is reactive, set_count is stable {value, _} = use_observable(_) → value is reactive Track stable_vars as a MapSet. When computing deps for a closure, subtract stable_vars from the captured variables. EXAMPLE — schematic output for a component with count (reactive) and set_count (stable): # Template: {@count} # Compiles to: use_memo([count], fn -> {:element, :span, [], [{:text, count}]} end) # Template: # on_click closure captures count (reactive) and set_count (stable) # deps = [count] (set_count excluded as stable) use_memo([count], fn -> {:element, :button, [on_click: fn -> set_count.(count + 1) end], [{:text, "+"}]} end) # Template: # closure captures only set_filter (stable) → deps = [] use_memo([], fn -> {:element, :button, [on_click: fn -> set_filter.(:all) end], [{:text, "All"}]} end) use_memo IS ALREADY DEFINED in lib/filament/hooks.ex. Read for exact signature. It takes (deps, fun) and returns the cached value if deps unchanged since last render (compared with ==). IMPLEMENTATION EXTENSION Extend lib/filament/vnode_compiler.ex (the file from Item 1a): - infer_scopes(vnode_ast, stable_vars) — wraps sub-expressions with use_memo - free_vars(ast) — collect variable references, excluding modules/fns/literals Modify compile/2 to call infer_scopes/2 after transform_at_assigns/1. The current wrap_in_use_memo/2 is a stub — replace it with the full algorithm. TESTING Run: mix test from repo root — all existing tests must pass. Write tests in test/filament/vnode_compiler_test.exs: 1. Warning suppression: compiling a template with a lexically-bound variable produces no IO output / warnings (capture IO.warn output and assert empty). 2. Memoization: render a component with @count twice — first with count=0, then count=0 again. The inner sub-expression (span containing count) must NOT be re-evaluated on the second render. Use a side-effect counter (e.g., Agent or :counters) inside the expression to detect evaluation. 3. Stable closure: render a component where on_click captures only set_count (stable setter). After two renders with the same count, the closure fn reference stored in the event handler must be === identical between renders. 4. Reactive closure: render a component where on_click captures count (reactive). After a render with count=0 and then count=1, the closure is re-evaluated (new fn reference), because count changed. 5. Separate scopes: a template with independent @count and @filter sub-expressions must produce two separate use_memo calls with their own deps, not one merged scope. Integration: after TodoList rewrite (Item 4), toggling one todo must NOT re-evaluate the VNode subtree for other todos — verify via the counter technique.
